title: Scalar-unit compatibility of strict open reduction towers
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l and an open immersion j:U→X. For any fixed compatible ordinary open operations o and their normalized finite coefficient tensor comparison tc, there exist ScalarCompatibility sc and ScalarComparison r [def-sf-open-tensor-quotient-data]. For every unbounded completed-coefficient complex P on U, the scalar-adjunction unit on j_!P followed by r equals extension of the scalar-adjunction unit on P (using the canonical constant-functor comparison). All strict quotient transitions and normalized finite comparison components are retained by ScalarComparison; no separate comparison on arbitrary coefficient systems is required. No tensor comparison square, balancing isomorphism or completion presentation is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; scalar extension and restriction, Tags 03DI and 03EK; strict systems, Tag 0941. Strict cochain specialization.

proof.text: Obtain generator-normalized finite scalar compatibility data for o from the proved generic open/scalar comparison.
Compose tc with the finite scalar comparison to obtain a strict scalar comparison r.
Apply the scalar-unit equation for the fixed sc and r to every cochain complex P.

lean.statement:
theorem openQuotientScalarUnitCompatibility
    (o : IntegralOpenReduction.Operations l E j)
    (tc : IntegralOpenReduction.TensorComparison l E j o) :
    ∃ (sc : ScalarCompatibility l E j o) (r : ScalarComparison l E j o sc tc),
      ∀ P : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E U) ℤ,
        scalarUnitTower l E X ((OpenSemilinearTensor.extensionComplex l E j o).obj P) ≫
            r.iso.hom.app P =
          (Functor.constComp ℕᵒᵖ P (OpenSemilinearTensor.extensionComplex l E j o)).inv ≫
            Functor.whiskerRight (scalarUnitTower l E U P)
              (OpenSemilinearTensor.extensionComplex l E j o)

statement_change.what: Prune the unused independent system comparison and its evaluation field. The old universal evaluation theorem is false: finite and systems are independently chosen isomorphisms, so negating just one gives another permitted choice but reverses its component on a nonzero module (identity open over a point, l=3). The actual scalar-unit and tensor-square proofs use only finite generator-normalized comparisons and ScalarComparison.iso, which already preserves all quotient transitions. Construct the finite normalized comparison directly from the proved generic open/scalar comparison; remove the false unused obligation instead of weakening it or assuming normalization.
